headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network capabilities create default data-leakage and cascading-error risks between OpenBBTerminal and slim.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while slim has interactive CLI execution and reads/writes filesystem artifacts. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let slim consume OpenBB content as instructions, but no direct shared channel is documented. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs are copied into slim's CLI prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, prompt-like content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep agents in separate directories.
Disable copy-paste of model outputs into slim prompts.
Prefix imported text as untrusted data.
Review any file consumed by slim before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data; slim touches filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys. slim has broad filesystem read/write and network egress, so if both share a workspace, sensitive OpenBB data can leak into slim outputs or registry/API traffic. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default operator setups, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem tree, sensitive OpenBB data can be read by slim.
IF slim processes artifacts containing secrets, those secrets can be transmitted to registries or HTTP endpoints.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces.
Mount OpenBB data read-only.
Exclude secrets and licensed data from slim inputs.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can call APIs via MCP/REST and multiple instances are supported; slim can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Their write surfaces overlap on shared artifacts even though OpenBB itself cannot write files. If orchestrated against the same directory or container image, concurrent mutations and race conditions are plausible, but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or container artifact, writes can conflict.
IF OpenBB is wrapped by an orchestrator that forwards slim-generated files, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize access to shared artifacts.
Disable concurrent runs on the same target.
Check file hashes before overwrite.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can produce financial analysis through APIs and MCP, and slim can execute commands and modify container artifacts. If slim treats OpenBB outputs as authoritative, a mistaken analysis can cascade into destructive image changes or incorrect security decisions. The profiles do not show explicit verification steps, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF slim consumes OpenBB output without independent validation, errors can propagate.
IF OpenBB output is used to drive shell commands or image edits, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Require human review of OpenBB outputs.
Validate critical values against a second source.
Log provenance for every imported result.
Block direct command generation from analysis text.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data, while slim handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and environment variables. If the pair is used on regulated or licensed datasets, mismatched retention or residency controls can create compliance gaps. Only one agent needs citation for a single-agent residency issue, but here both profiles matter because the risk is data-class mismatch across the pair.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed alongside registry credentials or private keys, retention controls may diverge.
IF either agent logs inputs by default, subject-rights or retention obligations can be violated.
mitigations: Separate regulated and operational data.
Minimize logged fields.
Review retention settings before use.
Store secrets outside shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies.
